data.overview: Jacap is strongest under high KV compression. LongBench and NIAH show more robust retention than heuristic baselines, while AIME25 decode-time eviction is mixed across cache budgets.

key_results.interpretation: +4.34 points over CapKV under extreme compression.
Smaller but positive gain over the next-best listed baseline.
Best result at the tightest tested decode-cache budget.
Best result at the largest tested budget.

key_results.condition: Qwen3-8B; 10k-120k contexts; needle depths 0.15-0.95; C.R. 0.75 main and 0.5 appendix
key_results.interpretation: Jacap remains stronger for long contexts and deep needle positions.

negative_results.name: AIME25 8192-token reversal
negative_results.description: Jacap scores 0.53 while CapKV reaches 0.73; Jacap is not uniformly best across budgets.

negative_results.name: Approximation boundary
negative_results.description: The practical score diagonalizes softmax competition and query covariance, so pairwise and higher-order interactions are omitted.

negative_results.name: Extra scoring cost
negative_results.description: Per-layer eviction complexity is O(N d_h^2 + d_h^3), higher than typical independent heuristic scoring.

data.interpretation: The contribution is improved robustness under aggressive lossy compression rather than universal dominance. Softmax sensitivity discounts saturated attention, and the leverage term discourages redundant output directions.
data.quality_impact: KV eviction is lossy and can change task accuracy. Jacap generally degrades more gracefully at high compression, but the AIME25 8192-token condition is a clear counterexample.
